title: Cherry-pick, and merge vs rebase
summary: Copy one commit to another branch with cherry-pick, and choose between merge and rebase for the history your team wants.

steps.title: cherry-pick: copy one commit
body: A fix landed on `main`, and the release branch needs it too, but not everything else on `main`:
```text
A---B---F---G   main          (F is the fix)
R1---R2   release/2.1
git switch release/2.1
git cherry-pick F
R1---R2---F'   release/2.1
Cherry-pick takes the **change** F made (its diff against its parent) and applies it here as a new commit F', with the same message and author.
- `git cherry-pick -x F` adds *(cherry picked from commit ...)* to the message, a useful trail on release branches.
- Conflicts work like merges: fix, `git add`, `git cherry-pick --continue` (or `--abort`).
- Cherry-pick ranges with `git cherry-pick A..B` (everything after A up to B).

steps.prompt: After `git cherry-pick F`, is the new commit F' the same commit as F?
options: No: same change and message, but a different parent, so a different hash
Yes, if there were no conflicts
steps.explain: That is why later merging both branches is fine (Git sees the same change twice and it merges cleanly) but `git log` shows two commits with the same message.

steps.title: Merge or rebase?
body: Both integrate work. They produce different histories:
```text
merge:   A---B---E---F---M   main          rebase:  A---B---E---F---C'---D'   main
C-------D   feature
| | Merge | Rebase |
| History | true record, with branch shape | linear, easier to read and bisect |
| Rewrites commits | no | yes (new hashes) |
| Safe on shared branches | yes | only for your own unpushed or private commits |
| Conflicts | resolved once, in the merge commit | possibly once per replayed commit |
A common team rule: **rebase your own branch onto `main` to stay current; merge (or squash-merge) the pull request into `main`.** Never rebase `main` itself.

items: Bring the latest `main` into my private feature branch before review
Integrate a finished, reviewed feature into shared `main`
Clean up my 6 messy local commits
Combine two long-lived branches that many people commit to
Keep an exact record of when work was integrated
Put my unpushed commits on top of what I just fetched

steps.prompt: Your team squash-merges every pull request. What ends up on `main`?
options: One new commit per pull request, containing all its changes; the branch's individual commits are not on `main`
Every commit from the branch, plus a merge commit
Only the last commit of the branch
A merge commit with two parents
steps.explain: Squash-merge (`git merge --squash` + commit, or the button on GitHub) keeps `main` to one commit per change. The cost: the feature branch's history is not preserved there.

steps.prompt: `main` has `A---B---F---G`, `release` has `A---B---R1`. You run the commands below. What does `git log --oneline` print? Write the picked commit with a prime.
steps.explain: Only F's change is copied, as a new commit on top of `release`. G stays on `main` only.

steps.prompt: Match the situation to the tool.
pairs: Backport one security fix to two release branches
Update my feature branch with the latest `main`

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: copy commit `9f8e7d6` onto this branch, recording where it came from; after resolving a conflict, carry on.
steps.explain: `-x` appends *(cherry picked from commit 9f8e7d6...)*, so anyone reading the release branch can find the original.

steps.title: Backport one fix with cherry-pick -x
prompt: Release `2.4` is out, and customers see VAT rounded wrongly. The fix, `Fix VAT rounding`, is on `main` in `~/shop`, between feature commits that must **not** go into the release.
2. Copy just that commit onto `release/2.4`, recording where it came from.

checks.name: release/2.4 has the fix on top
checks.fail: The newest commit on `release/2.4` should be `Fix VAT rounding`.

checks.name: the message records the original commit
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && git log -1 --format=%B release/2.4 | grep -qF "(cherry picked from commit $(cat /opt/dojo/state/fix))"
checks.fail: Use `-x`: it appends `(cherry picked from commit <hash>)`, so anyone can trace the backport.

checks.name: nothing else came along
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-list --count release/2.4)" = 2 && ! git cat-file -e release/2.4:src/Wishlist.cs 2>/dev/null && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s main)" = 'Limit wishlist size'
checks.fail: `release/2.4` should be its old commit plus the fix only, and `main` must be unchanged.

hints: `git log --oneline main` lists the commits; `git log --oneline --grep VAT main` finds the one you want.
Switch to the release branch first: `git switch release/2.4`.
solution: git cherry-pick -x "$(git log --format=%H --grep 'Fix VAT rounding' -1 main)"
steps.explain: Cherry-pick makes a **new** commit with the same change and a new hash. `-x` is the convention for backports to public branches: the line it adds lets `git log --grep` and reviewers connect the two. Fix on `main` first, then cherry-pick down, so the next release cannot lose the fix.
